card.name: Alkayida
card.tagline: Ghanaian Azonto-era street dance popularised by hiplife artist Guru
card.profile: Alkayida (also spelt Akayida) is a Ghanaian street dance emphasizing side-to-side moves, upper-body gestures and footwork-heavy freestyling, encouraging group routines and individual competition (Wikipedia). It emerged from Accra youth styling around 2013 and was popularised by hiplife artist Guru's song 'Akayida (Boys Abre)' (Wikipedia; Red Bull). The name controversially echoes 'Al-Qaeda'; Guru and other proponents insist on the spelling 'Akayida' and disavow any link to the terrorist organization, with the parenthetical 'Boys Abre' meaning 'boys are tired' (Wikipedia; Grandmother Africa).
card.insight: Afropop Worldwide noted that Alkayida tunes are markedly slower than Azonto with a pronounced one-two swing, distinguishing it from the earlier craze it was initially dismissed as an offshoot of (Afropop Worldwide).

lessons.distinctive_method: Breaking a single street dance down into three distinct layers: groove/bounce, arms, and body lean before putting them together.
